dmm-2005-team-01.title: Use the equation and Vieta
dmm-2005-team-01.body:
Every root $r$ satisfies $r^{17}=17r-17$. Adding over the 17 roots,
$$\sum r^{17}=17\sum r-17\cdot 17 .$$
The polynomial has no $x^{16}$ term, so by Vieta $\sum r=0$. Hence the sum is $-289$.

**Answer: $-289$**

dmm-2005-team-02.title: Height of the tetrahedron of centers
dmm-2005-team-02.body:
The centers form a regular tetrahedron of edge $2\cdot17=34$ m. Its height is $34\sqrt{\tfrac23}=\dfrac{34\sqrt6}{3}$.

The three lower centers are $17$ m above the ground, the top center is $\frac{34\sqrt6}{3}$ higher, and the top of the cow is another $17$ m above its center:
$$17+\frac{34\sqrt6}{3}+17=34+\frac{34\sqrt6}{3}\approx 61.76\text{ m}.$$

**Answer: $34+\frac{34\sqrt6}{3}$ m**

dmm-2005-team-02.title: Why the height is $a\sqrt{2/3}$
dmm-2005-team-02.body: A regular triangle of side $a$ has circumradius $a/\sqrt3$. The apex of the regular tetrahedron lies above the centroid at distance $a$ from each vertex, so $h^2=a^2-\frac{a^2}{3}=\frac{2a^2}{3}$, i.e. $h=a\sqrt{2/3}$. With $a=34$ this gives the same total.

dmm-2005-team-03.title: Find the period
dmm-2005-team-03.body:
$a_n$ is the last digit of $T_n=\frac{n(n+1)}2$. Since $T_{n+20}-T_n=20n+210$ is a multiple of $10$, the sequence of last digits has period $20$:
$$1,3,6,0,5,1,8,6,5,5,6,8,1,5,0,6,3,1,0,0,$$
whose sum is $70$. Since $1000=50\cdot20$, the total is $50\cdot70=3500$.

**Answer: 3500**

dmm-2005-team-04.title: Count the team-games
dmm-2005-team-04.body:
Each game involves two teams, so the total number of (team, game) appearances is $2\times(\text{number of games})$, an even number. But $15$ teams each playing $5$ games gives $15\cdot5=75$ appearances, which is odd. So no such tournament exists.

**Answer: 0**

dmm-2005-team-05.title: Factor out $\binom nk$
dmm-2005-team-05.body:
The general term is $(-1)^j2^{k-j}\binom nj\binom{n-j}{k-j}$. Since $\binom nj\binom{n-j}{k-j}=\binom nk\binom kj$ (choose $k$ people, then $j$ of them to be special), the sum is
$$\binom nk\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j\binom kj2^{k-j}=\binom nk(2-1)^k=\binom nk .$$
For $n=20,k=6$: $\binom{20}{6}=38760$.

**Answer: 38760**

dmm-2005-team-07.title: Telescoping
dmm-2005-team-07.body:
Use $k^3-1=(k-1)(k^2+k+1)$ and $k^3+1=(k+1)(k^2-k+1)$. The product splits into two telescoping products:
$$\prod_{k=2}^{100}\frac{k-1}{k+1}=\frac{1\cdot2}{100\cdot101}=\frac{1}{5050},\qquad
\prod_{k=2}^{100}\frac{k^2+k+1}{k^2-k+1}=\frac{100^2+100+1}{2^2-2+1}=\frac{10101}{3}=3367,$$
because $k^2+k+1=(k+1)^2-(k+1)+1$. So the value is $\frac{3367}{5050}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3367}{5050}$**

dmm-2005-team-08.title: Denest the radicals
dmm-2005-team-08.body:
$(\sqrt{3+\sqrt5}+\sqrt{3-\sqrt5})^2=6+2\sqrt{9-5}=10$, so the numerator is $\sqrt{10}$. Next $\sqrt{3-\sqrt8}=\sqrt2-1$ because $(\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2$. Hence the first fraction is $\frac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt2-1}=\sqrt{10}(\sqrt2+1)=2\sqrt5+\sqrt{10}$.

Also $\sqrt{8-2\sqrt{15}}=\sqrt5-\sqrt3$ because $(\sqrt5-\sqrt3)^2=8-2\sqrt{15}$, so the second fraction is $\frac{4}{\sqrt5-\sqrt3}=2(\sqrt5+\sqrt3)$.

The difference is $2\sqrt5+\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt5-2\sqrt3=\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt3$**

dmm-2005-team-10.title: Tangent doubling
dmm-2005-team-10.body:
The first three equations say $x=\dfrac{2w}{1-w^2}$, $y=\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}$, $z=\dfrac{2y}{1-y^2}$ (a denominator $1-w^2$ can't vanish, since then $2w=0$ would also be needed). The last says $w(1-z^2)=-2z$, i.e. $w=-\dfrac{2z}{1-z^2}$.

Write $w=\tan\theta$ (every real number is a tangent). By the double-angle formula $x=\tan2\theta$, $y=\tan4\theta$, $z=\tan8\theta$ and the last equation gives $w=-\tan16\theta$, i.e.
$$\tan\theta=\tan(-16\theta)\iff 17\theta\equiv0\pmod\pi\iff\theta=\frac{k\pi}{17}.$$
Because $\theta$ is only determined modulo $\pi$, $k=0,1,\dots,16$ gives exactly $17$ distinct values of $w=\tan\frac{k\pi}{17}$, none of which has $\tan$ undefined (since $17$ is odd, $\frac{k\pi}{17}\ne\frac\pi2$ mod $\pi$) and the later angles $2\theta,4\theta,8\theta$ also avoid $\frac\pi2$ mod $\pi$.

So the solutions are $(w,x,y,z)=\bigl(\tan\frac{k\pi}{17},\tan\frac{2k\pi}{17},\tan\frac{4k\pi}{17},\tan\frac{8k\pi}{17}\bigr)$, $k=0,\dots,16$; $k=0$ gives $(0,0,0,0)$.
